input:
I glance from Darkness's trembling back to Aqua's tear-streaked face, then to Megumin's napkin covered in explosion radii. One of them's a masochist who just found her dream quest, one's an alcoholic goddess running up our tab, and one's already spent her one contribution to the day.

"Darkness." I stand and jab a thumb toward the door. "You want those alligators so bad? Go scout the sewer entrance. Take Aqua with you — she can purify water or whatever. Just don't engage until I get there."

I point at Aqua before she can protest. "You're an Arch Priest. Undead, demons, giant sewer lizards — that's literally your job. Go earn your mid-shelf."

messages.content:
Darkness's chair screeches across the flagstones. She's on her feet before you finish the sentence, and for one suspended moment she simply stands there, gauntlets clenched at her sides, chest rising and falling in short, sharp breaths. Her face has gone the color of a sunset — not embarrassment exactly, but something hungrier, something she's trying very hard to bury beneath a mask of knightly duty. The mask isn't working. Her lips keep twitching at the corners.

Aqua lowers her mug with the slow, dawning horror of someone who just realized she's about to be left alone with the bill. The condensation from the cheap ale has soaked a ring into the tablecloth, and four empties now stand in a crooked row beside her elbow.

Megumin hasn't looked up from her napkin. She's added a second diagram — this one a cross-section of sewer architecture with annotated blast radii at various depths — because apparently the other twenty-three hours of her day are reserved exclusively for imagining the one spell she's already cast.

Behind the guild counter, Luna watches the exchange with the fixed, brittle smile of a woman mentally revising the morning's property damage estimate upward.

input:
I push back from the table and snag Megumin's napkin mid-diagram. "Come on. We're meeting the other two idiots at the sewers before Darkness gets herself happily drowned."

I toss a few coins at Luna on the way out — not enough to cover Aqua's tab, but it's the thought that counts.

messages.content:
The coins clatter across Luna's counter — three silver and a handful of copper that don't even cover half of Aqua's morning mead spree. Luna stares down at them with the hollow expression of a woman who has done this math too many times before.

You're already halfway to the door, Megumin's napkin crumpled in your fist. The archwizard herself stumbles after you, her legs still wobbling from this morning's Explosion. She grabs the back of your cloak to steady herself and nearly drags you both into a table full of junior adventurers, who scramble their chairs out of the way with practiced efficiency.

"Your tab," Luna calls from behind the counter, her professional smile audibly straining at the seams. She hasn't moved to pick up the coins yet. She's just looking at them. Counting. Re-counting. Hoping the math changes.

input: I push through the guild doors with Megumin's napkin still crumpled in my fist, dragging the wobbly archwizard behind me by one crimson sleeve. "Pick up your feet — Aqua and Darkness are already at the sewer grate and if I know Darkness, she's probably already trying to get herself eaten."

messages.content:
The guild doors bang open and the bright morning hits your face like a slap — all sun-bleached cobblestones and the distant clang of the blacksmith's hammer. Behind you, Megumin's boots scrape and stumble across the threshold, her legs still operating on borrowed time after her dawn Explosion. The napkin in your fist crackles with every squeeze, her meticulous blast-radius calculations now hopelessly wrinkled.

You drag her into the street, and the townsfolk part before you like water around a stone. A baker pulls his cart aside. Two junior adventurers flatten themselves against a wall, their eyes tracking Megumin's eyepatch with the wary respect owed to someone who once vaporized the viscount's abandoned summer home. She catches them staring and lifts her chin, summoning every scrap of dignity she can muster while being hauled by the sleeve like a misbehaving cat.

The sewer grate sits near the old fountain at the east end of the square — a rusted iron ring set into the flagstones, its cover already pried open. Even from here you can smell it: damp rot and something muskier, something alive. Aqua's blue hair ought to be visible from this distance. It isn't. But you can hear what sounds like a muffled argument echoing up from below.

Megumin's grip on your cloak tightens. She's winded, pale around the edges, and judging by the way her other hand is still twitching toward the napkin in your fist, she hasn't given up on that sewer diagram yet.

input:
The sewer grate is just ahead — rusted iron yawns open beside the old fountain, and that rank, living stench rolls up from below. I can hear Aqua's voice now, high and indignant, bouncing off wet stone somewhere down there.

I drag Megumin the last few paces and peer down into the dark.

"Oi! You two better not have started without us!"

messages.content:
The sewer stench hits you like a physical wall — rot and wet stone and something older, something that's been festering down here since before Axel was a town. Below, the murky water gleams with an oily sheen, catching the pale blue glow of Aqua's scepter light. For a moment that's all you see: warped reflections, dripping brickwork, the rusted rungs of the ladder vanishing into shadow.

Then you spot them.

Aqua is flattened against the sewer wall like a fresco of divine cowardice, her scepter clutched to her chest, both knees visibly knocking even from this angle. Her mouth is open — you can hear the tail end of whatever she's been shrieking, the sound swallowed by the dripping tunnel acoustics. Twenty feet beyond her, thigh-deep in the black water, Darkness advances with the slow, deliberate gait of a woman walking toward an altar. Her gauntlets hang loose at her sides. She's murmuring something you can't quite make out — a prayer, a plea, the fevered whisper of someone who's finally getting exactly what she asked for.

And there, just beyond the reach of Aqua's light: two amber eyes the size of dinner plates, floating motionless on the water's surface, watching Darkness's approach with prehistoric patience. The Brutal Alligator hasn't moved. It doesn't need to. It's waiting for her to come to it.

Megumin sways beside you, one hand braced on the fountain's crumbling rim, her crimson eyes struggling to focus on the scene below. The napkin in your fist — her precious blast-radius calculations — is already damp with sewer condensation and useless.

Kazumaaaa! She's not listening! I told her to stop and she just kept walking — that pervert is actually trying to get eaten! And that thing is HUGE! (Aqua's voice cracks upward through the grate, her scepter trembling in both hands as she presses herself harder against the slime-covered wall.)
messages.speaker: Aqua

messages.content: ...deliver unto me the trial I was forged to endure... let its jaws close around this unworthy body... (Darkness doesn't look up. Her prayer drifts back toward the grate in a breathless, almost reverent murmur as she takes another slow step through the black water.)
messages.speaker: Darkness

messages.content: She's actually praying for it. I knew Darkness was strange, but this is a new depth — literally and figuratively. Also, I cannot climb down a ladder right now. My legs are — I mean, I am simply conserving my power. (Megumin peers past you into the dark, her eyepatch slightly askew, wobbling on legs that have approximately zero Explosions left in them.)
messages.speaker: Megumin

input:
The alligator's already on her. I can hear the impact — metal screaming against teeth — and Aqua's shrieking hitting a pitch that could shatter glass.

I swing myself onto the ladder and start climbing down, fast.

"Hold on, you degenerate liability — I'm coming!"

messages.content:
The ladder rungs are slick with condensation and something you don't want to identify. Each downward step brings the chaos into sharper focus — the water below churning white where the alligator thrashes, Darkness's armored form clamped sideways in its jaws like a steel-wrapped chew toy, her legs trailing limply through the murk as the beast hauls her toward the deeper tunnel. She isn't fighting. Her sword still sits in its sheath, her gauntleted hands hanging at her sides, and the noise she's making is not a scream.

Aqua has pressed herself so hard against the slime-slick brickwork that she's practically become part of the wall. Her scepter lies abandoned in the shallows three feet away, its pale blue glow flickering across the rippling water, catching the oily rainbow sheen on the surface and the whites of her wide, unblinking eyes. She's staring at the alligator like it's the demon lord himself risen from the depths. Her mouth moves, but nothing coherent comes out.

Above you, Megumin's shadow blocks the sewer grate's light — she's peering down, one hand gripping the ladder frame, the other still clutching the soggy remains of her napkin diagram. Her legs are visibly shaking even from here.

D-don't... don't save me yet! I'm still... assessing its attack patterns! For tactical purposes! (Her voice quavers with something that is absolutely not fear, muffled through the alligator's teeth grinding against her breastplate.)
messages.speaker: Darkness

messages.content: She's enjoying this! Look at her face — she's enjoying this! This is a new kind of messed up even for her! (Points a trembling finger at Darkness, still pressed flat against the wall.)
messages.speaker: Aqua

messages.content: Kazuma! I cannot climb down — my legs are still recovering from this morning's magnificent Explosion! But if you need me to cast again, I could... theoretically... collapse the entire tunnel system! (Shouts from above, leaning dangerously over the grate opening.)
messages.speaker: Megumin
